findings.topic: Ownership and PID discovery must be executable, race-aware and bounded
findings.evidence: Proposal requires membership and invocation ancestry but has no reader or discovery algorithm. The capability receipt shows only /proc/1594/status prefix for the owned shell, not compiler process discovery or ancestry access.
findings.minimalRepair: Specify the owned container identity, guest boot identity, cgroup path/inode, namespace mapping and invocation root PID plus start-time. Enumerate only the owned cgroup subtree through bounded cgroup.procs reads, or demonstrate an equally confined method; never scan other lab process argv. Handle descendant cgroups or explicitly detect and mark them unsupported. Validate cgroup membership and stat start-time before and after identity/status reads; associate ancestry by PID plus start-time rather than PID alone. If parent disappears before validation, retain an unknown/gap rather than infer ancestry. Record owned-but-unattributed activity so it cannot silently masquerade as exclusive invocation activity. Define finite PID, subtree, argv and per-file read limits. No helpers per sample. No new privileges or changes to VM configuration.

findings.topic: Clock and launcher-boundary ordering require one explicit protocol
findings.evidence: Proposal provides monotonic brackets and one wall anchor. Existing launcher runs on macOS while an outside-container observer would run in the guest; these monotonic domains cannot be compared directly. Existing launcher uses synchronous child execution and has no boundary channel.
findings.minimalRepair: Use one guest monotonic domain for sample bounds and observer-received boundary markers, or retain a bounded synchronization handshake that expresses uncertainty. Record clock name/unit and guest boot/namespace identity. Bracket each actual read batch; define delta interval conservatively from the preceding read's earliest bound through the next read's latest bound. Do not compare host and guest monotonic numbers directly. Obtain the return-boundary sample before artifact-copy begins, with an explicit bounded acknowledgement or an explicit missing-boundary record. Any observer failure must not indefinitely block launcher completion, compiler stdout/stderr draining or postguards. Missed ticks create gaps without catch-up bursts.

findings.topic: Byte quotas bound retained data but do not yet demonstrate coverage or memory bounds
findings.evidence: 768KiB sample rows / approximately 2641 ticks from the old 264.017s run permits only about 298 bytes per tick before any slow memory.stat records. The specified full keyed fields, multiple process rows and slow records have no encoded schema or allocation budget yet. The 300s child limit does not cap total diagnostic duration.
findings.minimalRepair: Provide the exact compact schema and a static byte-budget calculation using retained process identities and representative keyed data, counting all new observation files, markers, dictionaries and summary. Define which quota owns slow memory.stat/pressure/local events and unknown keys. Bound input bytes, partial records, dictionary count and transient allocations before reading/serializing; a disk cap alone is insufficient. State the minimum useful expected observation horizon and the consequence of earlier truncation. No claimed guarantee of observing the entire run. Preserve all complete rows, reserve terminal/coverage bytes outside sample exhaustion, and never overwrite old evidence or ring-buffer away early events.

findings.topic: Partial capture and failure isolation need concrete behavior
findings.evidence: The proposal correctly stops only observation at quota exhaustion, but a reader crash, malformed read, permissions loss, broken pipe, full filesystem or parent disconnect could prevent its promised terminal summary or interfere with the launcher unless explicitly handled.
findings.minimalRepair: Use bounded incremental retention rather than keeping the sole trace in memory until exit. Reserve a launcher-owned terminal status path for observer exit/failure and last durable bounds when the observer cannot write. Distinguish unsupported optional files, transient vanished PIDs, incomplete reads, counter parse errors, missed ticks and output truncation. Never convert missing readings into zero or reuse stale process identity. Required evidence or ownership failure before verify blocks launch; a loss during verify marks coverage insufficient while healthy compiler and original postguards continue. No signals, suspension, reprioritization, extended timeout or whole-run timer.

findings.topic: Fresh epoch and immediate verify admission remain separate authority
findings.evidence: Existing epoch is nonzero and old launcher pins StartedAt=2026-10-25T23:29:57.087744357Z. This proposal explicitly grants no restart/reset/new-epoch authority. The original zeroMemory precheck occurs before staging, lock and check, so a later observation of an increment must not be ignored as permission to start verify.
findings.minimalRepair: Retain the old epoch and failure untouched. Any future fresh epoch needs its own explicit decision, exact identity binding and live zero counters plus original storage/idle/source/tool gates. A nonzero or incomplete mandatory counter reading immediately before verify blocks the single verify launch, even if an earlier precheck was zero. Preserve all keyed counter values, including future keys; strict acceptance never becomes delta-based. Compare epoch/cgroup identity before and after; identity change, reset/decrease or missing epoch makes evidence inadmissible. Remeasure 20GiB host and 11GiB guest pre-reserves, 10GiB post-reserves, configured VM/container limits and absence of concurrent owned SDK work. No stale snapshot or this SPEC approval substitutes for these checks.

inferenceAssessment.approved: Counter deltas bracket attempted memory-limit crossings; observed process identities support temporal overlap only. Zero oom does not erase max. RSS/HWM, cgroup peaks and memory.stat do not independently identify allocation causality. Cache state, observer overhead and unseen short-lived processes remain confounds.
inferenceAssessment.correctionForImplementation: Do not encode assumed tool order. Actual retained probe argv includes LexLeanProbe.P<semantic-prefix> and audit argv includes LexLeanAudit.A<semantic-prefix>; classify actual bounded argv against exact retained forms and pinned closure, not a loose basename guess. Ambiguous/unrecognized argv remains unknown.
allowedFindings: During identified compile/checker/audit/probe interval: directs static inspection of that exact retained generated module/import/tool path; no immediate remedy asserted.
Zero after verify then later increment: falsifies verify-only attribution in the new diagnostic only; does not establish Docker-copy charging.
Increment before verify: records earlier activity and prevents verify if mandatory immediate admission is nonzero.
No increment: non-reproduction in the new observed state only; old failure, product and control status remain unchanged.
Overlap, observer confound, missing identity, cap or partial data: insufficient attribution. No second run by default.
